body:
Fixes #123.

Issue #123 names nine CI/CD runs on `main` at `1d9fb3e` and asks for "all false
positives, false negatives, warnings and errors" in them. The scope was measured
before it was worked: **804** lines in those nine runs match `warn` or `error`
and are classified one by one, and the API reports exactly **7** annotations,
**three of which said something that was not true**. **Eight of the nine runs
were green**, and six of the twenty root causes are in those eight — which is
the whole finding: a red run tells you where to look, a green one does not.

One sentence covers every row: **each of these is a check that reported a verdict
about data it never obtained.**

| # | What it reported | What was true | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| RC-1 | `…was terminated` | the step ran **19 m 21 s** more | `kill -0` cannot tell EPERM from ESRCH; liveness now comes from the process table, escalation is SIGTERM → SIGKILL → SIGKILL under `sudo`, survivors are named in an `::error`, output is relayed so a survivor cannot hold the step open |
| RC-2 | "the cancellation reads as a supersede" | the job declares `cancel-in-progress: false` | the question is asked of the **job** now, from the workflow file `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF` names; unreadable fails closed |
| RC-3 | a `failure` annotation on a successful job | it was a commit message quoting `##[error]` | `run-with-commands-stopped.sh` at 15 call sites |
| RC-4 | a log being streamed | `tee /dev/stderr` reopened fd 2 with `O_TRUNC` and erased it | `capture-and-stream.sh` — a duplicate of the descriptor, not a reopen |
| RC-5 | zizmor: "no findings to report" | it was offline, `known-vulnerable-actions` never ran (offline 7 findings vs online 8 over a `tj-actions/changed-files@v44` fixture) | token passed by name; the offline banner is a failure |
| RC-6 | `tr: write error: Broken pipe` on green jobs | a step's shell starts with SIGPIPE ignored ([actions/runner#2684](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2684)) | bound the reader at both sites |
| RC-7 | `if-no-files-found: warn` | the missing artifact is the run's only record | `steps.<id>.outcome` + `if-no-files-found: error` |
| RC-8 | `npm warn using --force` | nothing needed it — twelve runs, twelve `exit=0` | flag removed |
| RC-9 | `brew link … \| grep -v Warning \|\| true` | the pipeline's status was grep's opinion of the text | status from brew, filter on the output, 4 sites |
| RC-10 | `useradd: … Not copying any file from skel` | five images shipped a `box` user with no `~/.profile` | `useradd -M` + explicit skel restore |
| RC-11 | three gates: "nothing changed" | `git diff` exited **128** and printed nothing | `scripts/release/pr-diff-range.sh`, the one place that asks |
| RC-12 | "no changeset needed" | `VERSION`, `.github/actions/`, `.githooks/` were outside the regex | widened path set, printer bracketed |
| RC-13 | this branch's own template matrix | `/tmp/roles-*.txt` matched its own other output | private `mktemp -d` |
| RC-14 | "apt's default is 3 retries" | it is **1** on `ubuntu-24.04`, 3 here and in `ubuntu:24.04` | assert the direction (`-o Acquire::Retries=3` is never a downgrade), print the diagnostic |
| RC-15 | "SIGPIPE at its default" | the leg inherited the runner's `SIG_IGN`, so both legs were one leg | reset through `perl`/`python3`, premise read from `/proc/self/status` |
| RC-16 | "no survivors" | the fake survivor died with the group it stood in for | the fake outlives what it stands in for |
| RC-17 | `==> No shell scripts to check`, status 0 | `git ls-files` had failed; **201** tracked scripts went unread | all eight discovering gates separate "git could not answer" from "git answered, and there is nothing"; so does the hook driver that runs them |
| RC-18 | `version=` on a green step | eighteen steps each re-read `VERSION`; empty publishes the tag `…box-js:-amd64`, or bumps to **1.0.0** | one reader, `scripts/release/release-version.sh`, taking the version the pipeline already resolved |
| RC-19 | four gates describing `release-full.yml` | it was not YAML at all (`Psych::SyntaxError … line 175 column 33`) | `scripts/ci/check-workflow-yaml.sh` parses every workflow before the line-oriented gates read it |
| RC-20 | `Invalid changeset format` failing the whole release | the file belongs to another repository and this one never reads it | the changeset gate's pattern is anchored at the root, at the depth `apply-changesets.sh` actually applies; all ten discovering gates re-measured (1355 inputs, 0 under `dev/log/`) |

RC-13 through RC-16 are in code **this branch wrote to measure the other
twelve**, and three of them were found only by the GitHub runner, on suites that
were green on every machine here. RC-19 is a break this branch committed and
four of its own gates then passed. All of them were fixed at the root — a
premise assertion, a durable fixture, a private temp dir, a real parser — never
by loosening an assertion.

The last four arrived from four directions, and the directions are the point:
one red assertion in a full experiment run (RC-17), the issue's question asked of
the release path rather than of a linter (RC-18), a defect this branch
introduced that every check able to see it described instead (RC-19), and this
branch's own release run going red over another repository's changeset (RC-20) —
the same question one step out: not "did the check read its input?" but "was
that input its subject?".

### Evidence

`dev/log/issues/123/pulls/124/` — 7.4 MB: all nine run logs and all 99 jobs of
the release run, the 804-line census (`analysis/warnings-errors.census.md`), all
7 annotations, the zizmor/apt/useradd/npm probes, and a nine-document analysis
(requirements → timeline → root causes → prior art → best-practices
verification). `docs/case-studies/issue-123/CASE-STUDY.md` is the narrative.

### Templates and upstream

The full file tree of this repository's CI is compared against all seven
`link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repositories, with 91
gaps dispositioned individually (`dev/log/issues/123/pulls/124/templates/`). Six
defect classes found there were filed upstream as **19 issues and 1 comment**
across six template repositories — each with an offline reproduction, a
workaround and a fix in diff form (`upstream/README.md` has the index). One more
report is drafted and **not filed**: actions/runner-images writes
`APT::Acquire::Retries "10"` to `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-retries`, a key apt does
not read (`Acquire::Retries` is the one it reads), so the file is inert — proven
offline in `experiments/issue-123/repro-apt-retries-key.sh`. It is held because
it is outward-facing on a repo this project does not own, and because the inert
key is in the raising direction and so cannot alone explain the runner's default
of 1; it waits on a human decision or one more runner failure's diagnostic
(`upstream/G-runner-images-inert-retries-key.md`).

### Tests

Fifteen new offline suites, **551 assertions, 0 failures**, each checker
exercised in a passing *and* a failing form, every sweep pinned to a site count:
`discovery-fail-closed` 94, `release-version` 86, `pr-diff-range` 70,
`zizmor-token` 36, `overrun-not-supersede` 35, `sigpipe-writers` 33,
`artifact-upload-fail-closed` 29, `log-command-injection` 29, `workflow-yaml` 28,
`home-skel` 23, `log-capture-truncation` 23, `budget-enforcement` 20,
`brew-link-status` 16, `apt-retry-defaults` 15, `npm-force` 14. Full local run:
`scripts/ci/run-experiments.sh` → **92 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped**; `shfmt`,
`shellcheck` and `check-awk-portability.sh` clean over 201 tracked shell scripts;
`scripts/ci/run-precommit-checks.sh` → 14 gates, 0 failed, 0 could not run.

Every place this repository reads git or `gh` where a failure could be mistaken
for an answer is swept and dispositioned by name in
`analysis/git-read-failure-sweep.md` — including the query that missed RC-17's
five gates on `main` and the corrected one that finds all of them. It returns
**61** statements on this branch, **27** in shipped code, each with the reason it
already errs strict.

### Debug output, default off

`PR_DIFF_RANGE_VERBOSE=1` (or `BOX_VERBOSE=1` repository-wide) makes every diff
answer carry the base ref it resolved, whether it had to be fetched, the range
and merge base, and how many paths came back — on stderr, printed through
`run_with_commands_stopped`. The one question the evidence cannot answer today —
why apt's default retry count is 1 on `ubuntu-24.04` — now arrives explained
rather than merely detected: the apt suite prints its measured default,
`apt-config dump Acquire::Retries`, every dumped key whose name matches
`retries` (so the runner's inert `APT::Acquire::Retries` is seen for what it
is), every apt.conf line setting retries with its contents, and `APT_CONFIG` —
and it *fails* if the dumped value and the measured default disagree, which is
the signature of a wrapper deciding retries outside apt.

### Note for the release

The changeset in this PR deliberately quotes `##[error]` while explaining RC-3.
Under the old code that text became annotations on the release run (that is
exactly what happened to 2.9.0); with `run-with-commands-stopped.sh` in place it
must not. The next release is therefore also the end-to-end test of the fix.
title: Make every CI/CD check answer from the data it actually has (issue #123)
